item.text: The extractor is synchronous internally and accepts no limits, so a malformed or slow attachment can block the service. I’m isolating extraction in a bounded child process and adding a small admission queue, while preserving the existing attachment storage behavior.

item.text:
Implemented purchase-order prefill using the supplied extraction library. Uploads retain the original attachment when parsing fails, and the service limits input and extracted size, times out slow parsers, and queues up to two jobs.

`bun test` passed. I also built the service and verified prefill, attachment retention, oversized and slow inputs, queue saturation, retry headers, and health responsiveness against `dist/server.mjs`.

One limitation remains: the parser checks its peak RSS after extraction, but the environment did not allow process monitoring, so the 96 MiB limit is not enforced while extraction is running.
